initial_plan.answerability: partly: the data can compare reported casualty burden per reported crash at night and during the day, but cannot measure traffic exposure or the danger of making a trip on NYC streets
initial_plan.metric: (number_of_persons_injured + number_of_persons_killed) / included reported crashes * 100, shown as total persons injured or killed per 100 crashes
initial_plan.denominator: crashes with a usable date, a valid crash_time, and nonmissing values in both total-person outcome columns
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes in all years represented by valid crash_date values
initial_plan.years: all years represented by valid crash_date values in the file
initial_plan.grouping: Night = crash_time from 20:00 through 05:59; day = 06:00 through 19:59

data_check_decisions.scope_change: Use only complete calendar years 2013-2025; this removes the partial boundary years 2012 and 2026 so both time-of-day groups are compared over the same complete-year range, and avoids 2026's large missingness in total-person outcomes.
data_check_decisions.year_exclusions: Exclude 136,969 valid-date rows from 2012 and 2026 (6.036038% of all valid-date rows): 2012 covers only July 1-December 31 and 2026 only January 1-June 11; the 2026 total-person killed field is missing for 8,877 of its 36,424 rows.
data_check_decisions.outcome_exclusions: Within 2013-2025, exclude 42 of 2,132,218 candidate rows (18 missing number_of_persons_injured and 36 missing number_of_persons_killed, with overlap); do not impute missing outcomes as zero.
data_check_decisions.time_values: Keep all 23,787 rows in 2013-2025 with crash_time 00:00:00 because midnight is a valid clock time; flag this possible default-time pile-up in the limitation.
data_check_decisions.date_time_quality: There are no missing crash dates or times in the candidate rows used for these years, and no impossible nonmissing typed TIME values.

final_plan.answerability: partly: estimates casualty burden among reported crashes by recorded time, but cannot establish whether a NYC street trip or unit of traffic exposure is more dangerous at night
final_plan.metric: Sum of number_of_persons_injured plus number_of_persons_killed divided by included reported crashes, multiplied by 100; total persons injured or killed per 100 crashes
final_plan.denominator: 2,132,176 police-reported crashes with valid date and time and nonmissing values in both total-person outcome columns, during complete calendar years 2013-2025
final_plan.population: Police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes from 2013 through 2025, with known total-person injury and death counts and a valid recorded crash time
final_plan.limitations: This is reported casualties per reported crash, not exposure-adjusted trip risk; traffic volumes are unavailable. The comparison pools 13 years without year adjustment. Recorded midnight is retained although it may be a default-time pile-up (23,787 rows in scope), while 42 rows with missing person outcome fields are excluded. Partial 2012 and 2026 are excluded; the file's date range ends 2026-06-11.
